authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: DHT Bauhinia, a 2007-built VLCC, was delivered to its new owner. The Company booked a gain of $34.2 million on the sale in the third quarter.
The Company took delivery of the newbuilding VLCC DHT Impala, the fourth and final newbuilding delivered in 2026. The vessel entered the spot market.
The Company entered into time charter agreements for DHT Jaguar and DHT Panther with global energy companies. These are new employment contracts for those two vessels.
no_value_reason: some filed figures are years older than the latest annual report

business_model.claim: DHT sells crude oil transportation. It owns and operates a fleet of 23 VLCC crude oil tankers, all wholly owned, with two of them agreed to be sold at the 20-F date.
quotes: As of March 13, 2026, our fleet consisted of 23 VLCC crude oil tankers (including two VLCCs that we have agreed to sell), all of which are wholly owned by DHT Holdings, Inc.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from two employment forms: time charter hire and vessels trading in the spot market. Time charters give more predictable cash flow, and spot trading gives less predictable revenue with more upside when rates improve.
quotes: Our revenues are principally derived from time charter hire and by vessels operating in the spot market.
Vessels operating in the spot market generate revenues that are less predictable but may enable us to capture increased profit margins during periods of improved rates.

business_model.claim: The fleet is split between the two forms. At the 20-F date 11 of 23 vessels were on time charters and 12 were in the spot market. Spot exposure in Q3 2026 was 51.2%.
quotes: As of the date of this report, 11 of our 23 vessels are on time charters and 12 vessels are operating in the spot market.

business_model.claim: Customers are oil-market companies, mostly described as global energy companies, and revenue is concentrated. The five largest customers were 61%, 61% and 73 % of revenue in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
quotes: In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our five largest customers together represented 61%, 61% and 73 % of our revenue, respectively.
under contracts concluded with global energy companies

business_model.claim: DHT reports one segment. Operating the tanker fleet is the primary business, and technical management services are a secondary activity that produced only $1.2 million of other revenues in 2025.
quotes: The Company is organized and managed as one segment based on the nature and financial effects of the business activities in which it engages and the economic environment in which it operates.
Other revenues for 2025 were $1.2 million compared to $3.9 million in 2024 and relate to technical management services provided.

business_model.claim: Revenue depends on the number of revenue days and the rate earned per day. Shipping revenues fell $70.6 million in 2025, with $40.1 million from fewer revenue days after the fleet shrank and $30.4 million from lower revenue per day.
quotes: Shipping revenues decreased by $70.6 million, or 12.4%, to $497.2 million in 2025 from $567.8 million in 2024.
The decrease from 2024 to 2025 includes $40.1 million attributable to a decrease in total revenue days resulting from a smaller fleet size and $30.4 million attributable to lower revenue per day.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item, with the mechanism stated by management
business_model.claim: Freight rates were the main driver in 2026. Q3 2026 shipping revenues were 332.1 (table in USD millions) against 107.2 in Q3 2025, and the VLCC spot rate per day was $167,100 against $38,700. Management attributes the strength to logistical disruptions and longer transport distances.
quotes: The freight market remains strong due to ongoing logistical disruptions resulting in operational inefficiencies, in combination with shifting crude procurement patterns expanding transportation distances.

business_model.claim: Forward rates remained high for Q4 2026. As of the 6-K, 68% of available spot days were booked at an average of $579,900 per day.
quotes: Thus far in the fourth quarter of 2026, 68% of the available VLCC spot days have been booked at an average rate of $579,900 per day on a discharge-to-discharge basis.

business_model.claim: Costs are mainly voyage expenses (bunkers and port charges), vessel operating expenses, interest, depreciation and G&A. Voyage expenses move with how many vessels trade spot, falling to $128.1 million in 2025 from $179.6 million.
quotes: Our expenses consist primarily of voyage expenses, including primarily the cost of bunkers and port charges; vessel operating expenses, hereunder crew cost, maintenance expenses, spare parts, various consumables, insurance premium expenses; interest expense, financing expenses, depreciation expense, impairment charges, vessel taxes and general and administrative expenses.
The decrease was mainly due to fewer vessels operating in the spot market during 2025 compared to 2024, which led to a reduction in voyage expenses.

business_model.claim: Vessel operating costs track fleet size. They were $73.0 million in 2025 against $78.6 million, and the vessel-owning subsidiaries pay the actual cost of technical management by the in-house manager.
quotes: Vessel operating expenses decreased by $5.6 million to $73.0 million in 2025 from $78.6 million in 2024.
The relevant vessel-owning subsidiary pays the actual cost associated with the technical management.

business_model.claim: Financing cost is a variable cost driver. All secured credit facility debt bore SOFR-based interest at year-end 2025. Interest expense fell by $16.2 million in 2025 on lower rates, and total debt was $428.7 million.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, all of our obligations under the secured credit facilities bear interest by reference to the Secured Overnight Finance Rate (“SOFR”).
We had $428.7 million of total debt outstanding at December 31, 2025, compared to $409.4 million at December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: Fleet renewal adds to profit through vessel-sale gains and requires heavy capital spending. In 2025 DHT booked a $52.9 million gain on sales of older vessels, and the four 2026 newbuildings average $130.3 million each.
quotes: The Company recorded a gain of $52.9 million in 2025 related to the sale of DHT Scandinavia, DHT Lotus and DHT Peony.
The average price for the four ships is $130.3 million, adjusted for change orders.

business_model.claim: Profits are returned through a payout policy of 100% of ordinary net income as quarterly dividends. A $1.45 per share dividend was declared for Q3 2026.
quotes: our board of directors revised the dividend policy to return 100% of our ordinary net income to shareholders in the form of quarterly cash dividends

business_model.claim: Market cyclicality underlies the whole model. Demand and supply of tanker capacity, vessel values and charter rates all swing, and this feeds the revenue line directly.
quotes: The tanker industry historically has been highly cyclical.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 (fleet description) and P2 (technical management by Goodwood)
competitive_position.claim: DHT is a pure-play crude tanker owner. Its fleet is entirely VLCCs, 23 of them with a combined 7,162,399 dwt and an average age of 10.1 years as of the annual report date. Technical management is carried out in-house by a subsidiary.
quotes: We operate a fleet of crude oil tankers.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P8 and P5; the scrubber detail is stated in P1
competitive_position.claim: DHT is renewing its fleet. It has sold its oldest vessels (DHT Bauhinia was delivered to its new owner in the third quarter). It took delivery of the fourth and final newbuilding of the 2026 series, and says the program is fully funded. A further Hanwha VLCC order was added after quarter-end.
quotes: The newbuilding program has been fully funded

competitive_position.basis: stated in P5 and P6; the market-versus-company split is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Recent earnings are very strong. Third-quarter average combined time charter equivalent earnings were $141,300 per day, and profit after tax was $270.9 million against 44.8 (table in USD millions) in the year-earlier quarter. The company attributes this to robust tanker market conditions and strong commercial performance.
quotes: The freight market remains strong due to ongoing logistical disruptions resulting in operational inefficiencies, in combination with shifting crude procurement patterns expanding transportation distances.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P5; the mechanism is stated in P3
competitive_position.claim: DHT keeps a mix of spot and time charter employment. Spot exposure was 51.2% in the latest quarter versus 76.4 % in the prior full year. For the next quarter, 68% of available spot days were booked at $579,900 per day, which indicates strong customer demand for its ships.
quotes: Thus far in the fourth quarter of 2026, 68% of the available VLCC spot days have been booked at an average rate of $579,900 per day on a discharge-to-discharge basis.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P5; the framing against profit is inferred
competitive_position.claim: The balance sheet is conservative relative to earnings. At the end of the third quarter, interest-bearing debt was 498.7, cash was 154.7 and net debt was 344.0 (table in USD millions), while the quarter's profit was $270.9 million. The company describes its capital structure as one that promotes staying power through the business cycles.
quotes: our prudent capital structure that promotes staying power through the business cycles

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 as management's outlook; it is a management view, not an independent measure
competitive_position.claim: Management sees the supply side as favourable. It says the global tanker fleet is ageing with limited new supply. The orderbook is some 22% of capacity over five years, against close to 50% of the fleet projected to be older than 15 years by the end of 2026. Sanctions and emissions regulation are also expected to constrain older ships.
quotes: The global tanker fleet continues to rapidly age with limited new supply entering the market.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P5 as management commentary
competitive_position.claim: Geopolitical disruption supports freight rates but is outside DHT's control. The company notes that a full or partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz has been shown to be possible. It also expects energy-security restocking to boost transport demand.
quotes: Geopolitical risks persist because recent events demonstrated for the first time in history that a full or partial closure of the Strait of Hormuz is possible, altering long-term risk perceptions even if regular traffic resumes.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3, P5 and P2; the net effect on DHT is not stated
competitive_position.claim: Market structure is shifting toward consolidation by private aggregators. Management expects this to tighten availability and shift pricing, and sees a possible premium for reliability. The risk factors also warn that consolidation among DHT's customers could reduce its bargaining power.
quotes: This consolidation will likely shift the pricing dynamics and put pressure on timely availability of ships.

competitive_position.claim: Customer concentration is a threat. Five customers represent the majority of revenue, and their share rose to 73 % in the latest annual period from 61% in each of the two prior years.
quotes: Five customers represent the majority of our revenue.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1; the commodity framing is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Competition is mainly on price, and DHT competes with other tanker owners and with fleets controlled by its customers. Vessel condition, location, size, age and reputation also affect its position.
quotes: We primarily compete for charters on the basis of price

competitive_position.claim: The tanker cycle and spot-market exposure remain core threats. Charter rates and vessel values are volatile, and 12 vessels were in the spot market as of the annual report date.
quotes: The tanker industry historically has been highly cyclical.

competitive_position.claim: Loan covenants limit flexibility and tie DHT to vessel values. Credit facilities generally require vessel market value of at least 135% of the loan amount, and a fall in vessel values could force repayments.
quotes: Our credit facilities generally require that the fair market value of the vessels pledged as collateral never be less than 135% of the aggregate principal amount outstanding under the loan.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the unaudited balance sheet in the Q3 6-K and the audited 20-F balance sheet.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity at the latest quarter-end is ample against short-term obligations. Cash was $154,726 (table in thousands), up from 79,034 at the prior year-end. Current assets of $380,458 compare with current liabilities of $94,262.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the Q3 results table and in the 20-F MD&A.
financial_health.claim: Gross debt has risen while net debt is roughly flat. Interest-bearing debt was 498.7 and net debt 344.0 (table in USD millions) at the latest quarter-end. At the 2025 year-end they were 428.7 and 349.7.
quotes: We had $428.7 million of total debt outstanding at December 31, 2025, compared to $409.4 million at December 31, 2024.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the Q3 6-K balance sheet; the comparison is a plain reading of two printed lines.
financial_health.claim: Balance-sheet leverage is moderate. Total liabilities were $549,524 against total equity of $1,404,629 (table in thousands) at the latest quarter-end.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 20-F cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow was strong in 2025 but lower than in 2024. Net cash provided by operating activities was 276,650 (table in thousands), against 298,654 in 2024.

financial_health.basis: Inferred from the 20-F cash flow and income statement lines.
financial_health.claim: Reported 2025 profit was partly non-cash, but cash conversion was high. Profit for the year was 210,962, and operating cash flow of 276,650 was higher. Depreciation of 106,370 was added back and the gain on sale of vessels of (52,943) was removed.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 20-F cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Self-funding in 2025 came with heavy reinvestment and debt turnover. Investing activities used (166,421), including investment in vessels under construction of (198,511). Debt of 298,023 was issued and (281,066) repaid.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 results release.
financial_health.claim: Earnings power rose sharply in 2026. Adjusted EBITDA was 269.5 in the latest quarter (table in USD millions) versus 57.7 a year earlier. Ordinary net income of $234.5 million excludes a $34.2 million sale gain and a $2.2 million non-cash derivative gain.
quotes: After adjusting for the $34.2 million gain on sale of DHT Bauhinia and the non-cash fair value gain related to interest rate derivatives of $2.2 million, the Company had ordinary net income for the quarter of $234.5 million, equating to $1.45 per basic share.

quotes: the facility has final maturity in January 2027
The resulting net drawdown of $56 million, together with the final installment of $3.7 million, is due in the first quarter of 2027.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 20-F text; the swap and facility details were disclosed as of early 2026.
financial_health.claim: Other known maturities lie further out. The Credit Agricole facility has a final payment of $22.5 million in December 2028, and eight amortizing interest rate swaps totalling $200.6 million mature in the fourth quarter of 2028.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the Q3 6-K and the 20-F.
financial_health.claim: The company says it can meet maturities from cash, operating cash flow and re-borrowing. In the fourth quarter it prepaid $59.1 million and $26.5 million under two Nordea facilities, and these amounts remain available for re-borrowing.
quotes: The prepaid amounts remain available for re-borrowing under the terms of the respective facilities, which have not been cancelled.
We believe that our working capital is sufficient for our present requirements.

quotes: Our credit facilities generally require that the fair market value of the vessels pledged as collateral never be less than 135% of the aggregate principal amount outstanding under the loan.
unencumbered consolidated cash shall be at least the higher of (i) $30 million and (ii) 6% of our gross interest-bearing debt

quotes: The newbuilding program has been fully funded

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited item (rate table and highlights).
growth_thesis.claim: Higher VLCC freight rates are the main driver of recent earnings growth: spot earnings reached $167,100 per day in the latest quarter against $38,700 a year earlier, and combined time charter equivalent earnings were $141,300 per day. For this to continue, the logistical disruptions and longer crude transport distances that management cites must persist.
quotes: The freight market remains strong due to ongoing logistical disruptions resulting in operational inefficiencies, in combination with shifting crude procurement patterns expanding transportation distances.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited item (outlook section).
growth_thesis.claim: Near-term earnings visibility rests on fourth-quarter bookings already made: 68% of available spot days are booked at an average of $579,900 per day. This holds only if those voyages are completed and the remaining spot days are booked at comparable levels.
quotes: Thus far in the fourth quarter of 2026, 68% of the available VLCC spot days have been booked at an average rate of $579,900 per day on a discharge-to-discharge basis.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by management in the cited items; the outlook is management's view, not a measured result.
growth_thesis.claim: Tight tanker supply supports the rate environment. The 20-F cites an orderbook of some 22% of capacity over five years against an ageing fleet, and the latest 6-K cites limited effective fleet supply growth. This requires newbuilding deliveries to stay limited and older ships to keep losing productivity.
quotes: The orderbook for supply of new ships is benign with some 22% of capacity scheduled for delivery over the coming five years.
Limited effective fleet supply growth due to an aging fleet, a growing share of vessels operating outside mainstream trades, and a limited near-term newbuilding delivery schedule.

growth_thesis.claim: The fleet renewal programme adds modern capacity: the fourth and final 2026 newbuilding was delivered, $521.1 million has been paid on the programme, and a further VLCC was ordered. This depends on the remaining funding and deliveries proceeding as stated.
quotes: The newbuilding program has been fully funded
In November 2026, the Company entered into an agreement with Hanwha Ocean Co., Ltd. for the construction of a VLCC.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited items; the 20-F risk factor states the divestment intent.
growth_thesis.claim: Selling the oldest ships funds renewal and adds gains. DHT Bauhinia was delivered to its buyer with net cash proceeds of $51.0 million and a gain of $34.2 million. This requires buyers to keep paying prices above book value for older tonnage.
quotes: On July 20, 2026, DHT Bauhinia, built in 2007, was delivered to its new owner.

growth_thesis.claim: Fixed-rate time charters add a contracted base: DHT Jaguar and DHT Panther were fixed for three years at $75,000 and $100,000 per day. This requires charterers to perform, and the 20-F notes that a limited number of customers provide most of the revenue.
quotes: The vessels were fixed at rates of $75,000 per day and $100,000 per day, respectively, under contracts concluded with global energy companies.
Five customers represent the majority of our revenue.

growth_thesis.basis: Debt figures are stated in the 6-K table. The covenant is stated in the 20-F. The link to growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Balance-sheet capacity is a condition for continued growth. At the latest quarter-end interest-bearing debt was 498.7, cash was 154.7 and net debt was 344.0 (table in USD millions). The credit facilities require vessel collateral value of at least 135% of the loan outstanding, so growth depends on staying within the covenants.
quotes: Our credit facilities generally require that the fair market value of the vessels pledged as collateral never be less than 135% of the aggregate principal amount outstanding under the loan.

growth_thesis.basis: Revenue and net profit stated in the 20-F text. The attribution to gains and lower interest is inferred from the income statement lines and the MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: The prior-year baseline shows the growth is recent and rate-driven. Shipping revenues fell 12.4%, from $567.8 million to $497.2 million, on a smaller fleet and lower revenue per day. Profit still rose to $211.0 million from $181.5 million, helped by sale gains and lower interest cost. The growth therefore depends on the rate and fleet changes described above, not on a steady trend.
quotes: Shipping revenues decreased by $70.6 million, or 12.4%, to $497.2 million in 2025 from $567.8 million in 2024.
